elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language states that “Customer may terminate this Agreement ... for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate any Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added language states that Customer may terminate “any Order Form for convenience.”

elements.element: Customer’s termination for convenience requires 30 days’ prior written notice to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “30 days’ prior written notice to Vendor.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees allocable to the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Vendor must “refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination,” which operates as the required pro-rata refund.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that “Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.”
The clause expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right for the Agreement or any Order Form.

elements.element: Customer’s termination for convenience requires between 60 and 90 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only 30 days’ notice, not notice within the fallback range of 60–90 days.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer must not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so there is no fee exceeding the permitted cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The clause bars Vendor termination for convenience during a committed term but does not affirmatively grant or confine such a right to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor’s termination for convenience requires 90 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: No Vendor termination-for-convenience notice period is stated.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives a convenience right on 30 days’ written notice, prepaid post-termination fees are refundable, and Vendor is barred from terminating for convenience during a committed term. The change is targeted and preserves the existing cause-based termination rights. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its 60–90-day Customer notice period and Vendor end-of-term right on 90 days’ notice are absent.
